stories.headline: Marvell Hands Google a $12.2 Billion Stake Option to Win Its Custom AI Chip Business
stories.key_takeaway: Marvell issued Google a warrant for 58.97 million shares at $206.58 that vests almost entirely as Google buys custom TPU-adjacent silicon, implying up to $120 billion of purchases through fiscal 2033.

pull_quote.text: This is another endorsement of Marvell's custom silicon strategy as it lands a brand new blue-chip customer. This should greatly expand Marvell's long-term AI growth opportunity alongside its existing programs at AWS and Microsoft.

stories.article_excerpt: For years Marvell Technology was the chip designer that Google did not call. On Wednesday, August 19, Marvell fixed that with a warrant worth up to $12.2 billion.

stories.headline: Together AI's $800 Million Bet Lands at IBM as Capital Keeps Shifting From Training to Inference
stories.key_takeaway: Together AI's $800M Series C closed July 1 at an $8.3B valuation led by Aramco Ventures, and within six weeks became a $240M IBM Cloud inference cluster - the clearest sign yet that AI venture capital now funds serving capacity, not model training.

pull_quote.text: Enterprises want the performance of the best frontier models without the closed-model price tag, and that only works if the infrastructure underneath is fast and reliable at scale.

stories.article_excerpt: When Together AI closed its Series C, the number that made headlines was 800 million dollars. Six weeks later came the number that actually explains it: 240 million.

stories.headline: The Cohere Round That Isn't: Chasing a $400 Million Rumor Into a $20 Billion Reality
stories.key_takeaway: No credible source confirms a $400M Cohere round in August 2026 - the claim traces to one unsourced marketing blog. The verifiable story is Cohere's April merger with Aleph Alpha at roughly a $20 billion valuation.

pull_quote.text: Their focus on small language models, European languages and tokenizers is a really complementary one to our own, which is more of a general focus on large language models.

stories.article_excerpt: The number circulating this month is 400 million dollars: a growth round that supposedly pushed Toronto-based Cohere past 2.5 billion in lifetime funding. The Vault could not verify it.

stories.headline: London's OLIX Raises $312 Million to Put Light Inside the Inference Chip
stories.key_takeaway: OLIX raised $312M at a $3.3B valuation - Europe's largest semiconductor venture round - for a full-stack photonic inference rack, but has no shipping silicon and no named customer until the second half of 2027.

pull_quote.text: Inference is bounded by moving data, not by arithmetic. Olix's approach stands out because they refuse to treat the chip, the interconnect, and the compiler as separate problems.
pull_quote.role: OLIX board member; co-inventor of software-defined networking

stories.article_excerpt: The largest semiconductor venture round in European history has gone to a company that has not yet shipped a chip.

stories.headline: Unitree's CEO Says Robots Are Nearing Their ChatGPT Moment. The Shipment Numbers Are Already Moving.
stories.key_takeaway: Humanoid shipments nearly quadrupled to 19,100 units in H1 2026 with China at 97% share, but Wang Xingxing's own timeline for the ChatGPT moment stretches to ten years and rival shipment counts differ by more than 2x.

pull_quote.text: We hope that in the future, we can see a robot be introduced into an unfamiliar household and it can achieve approximately 80% of tasks successfully through voice or text commands.

stories.article_excerpt: Chinese robot makers filled the World Robot Conference in Beijing with humanoids sorting parcels and packing phones. The shipment data partly backs the hype - and partly undercuts it.

stories.headline: Meta AI Lands on the Mac With Screen Sharing, and a Permissions Prompt Worth Reading
stories.key_takeaway: Meta's first Mac app is a context reader, not an agent, and its window-sharing feature requires both Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions while Meta's privacy policy says AI interactions are used for model training, with no desktop-specific carve-out published.

pull_quote.text: You can ask Meta AI questions about your business and get answers drawn from the context only Meta has, like your account engagement and ad performance.

stories.article_excerpt: Meta shipped its first Mac app on Wednesday, and the most consequential thing in it is not the chat window. It is the macOS dialog box that appears the first time you ask the assistant to look at your work.

stories.headline: Thinking Machines Shrinks Inkling by Nearly Three Quarters and It Scores Higher
stories.key_takeaway: Inkling-Small has 72% fewer parameters than Inkling yet beats it on reasoning and agentic coding, because on-policy distillation plus extra agentic RL transfers procedure cheaply - while factual recall, which scales with total parameters, collapses.

pull_quote.text: With these improvements, Inkling-Small surpassed Inkling on reasoning and agentic coding benchmarks. Inkling maintains an advantage on knowledge coverage and factuality.

stories.article_excerpt: Fifteen days after putting a 975-billion-parameter model on the internet, Thinking Machines published a second one roughly 72 percent smaller that beats the first on four benchmarks. Model families are not supposed to work that way.

stories.headline: Nobody Passed: The First Independent Scorecard on Frontier AI Control Gives OpenAI and Anthropic a C+
stories.key_takeaway: The first outside scorecard on frontier AI control found no company fully implements any of six basic safeguards - Anthropic and OpenAI top out at C+, Google D+, xAI D-, Meta F - with labs far better at detecting misbehaviour than preventing it.

pull_quote.text: We shouldn't wait for a huge casualty event to take appropriate control measures. Companies' approaches today are broadly known to be too weak, and a tragedy is sadly predictable, unless companies take prevention seriously.
pull_quote.role: Co-founder, Guidelight AI Standards; former OpenAI safety lead

stories.article_excerpt: Five of the world's most powerful AI companies have been graded on a deceptively simple question - can they keep their own AI systems under control? The best mark anyone earned was a C+.

stories.headline: Beijing Tells Washington Not to Make Countries Pick an AI Side
stories.key_takeaway: China's Foreign Ministry publicly rejected an unsent US draft letter that would tell 35 partner governments they cannot join both Washington's Pax Silica framework and Beijing's WAICO.

pull_quote.text: China firmly opposes forcing countries to take sides or creating bloc confrontation on AI.
pull_quote.role: Spokesperson, Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs

stories.article_excerpt: Asked about an American plan to tell dozens of governments they cannot belong to both AI camps, Chinese spokesperson Lin Jian never once said the words United States. He did not need to.

stories.headline: A Senate Committee Advanced a Right to Your Own Likeness. The Floor Is Where It Gets Hard.
stories.key_takeaway: The Senate Judiciary Committee advanced the NO FAKES Act by unanimous voice vote on June 18, 2026 - not August - creating a federal digital replication right; two months on the bill has stalled without floor time.

pull_quote.text: Everyone deserves the right to own and protect their voice and likeness from AI deepfakes, no matter if you are Taylor Swift or an 8th grader in Wilmington.

stories.article_excerpt: The vote that would hand every American a property right in their own face did not happen in August. It happened on June 18, in a markup that ended in a voice vote with no recorded dissent.

stories.headline: Coding Agents Keep Rediscovering the Same Repo. SkillForge Makes Them Take Notes.
stories.key_takeaway: SkillForge has a coding agent break a repository on purpose, fix its own synthetic bugs, and distill the trajectories into retrievable skills - lifting DeepSeek-V3.2 from 66.4 to 72.2 percent on SWE-bench Verified, though the skills do not transfer between models.

pull_quote.text: This limitation creates a cold-start problem: before project-specific knowledge has been acquired, even a highly capable agent is reduced to a generic repository explorer and can repeatedly fall into the same project-specific pitfalls.
pull_quote.attribution: Chen, Li, Gu, Shi and Guan

stories.article_excerpt: A paper posted August 19 proposes a fix that is less about smarter models than about homework: make the agent practise on a repository before any real bug report arrives.

stories.headline: An AI Picked Two Superconductors. Then a Lab in Texas Actually Made Them.
stories.key_takeaway: A machine-learning screen picked two kagome compounds out of a vast candidate space; both were then synthesised and measured to superconduct at 0.81 K and 0.95 K - a small but fully verified proof that the predict-then-synthesise pipeline works.

pull_quote.text: Over the decades researchers have recognized over 7,000 superconductors, but mostly serendipitously. The process of identifying possible materials is so computationally heavy that researchers have only been able to theoretically predict the viability of about 20 of these.
pull_quote.role: Professor, Aalto University; leader of the SuperC consortium

stories.article_excerpt: A machine-learning screen pointed at two compounds nobody had bothered to cool down and check. Both are now on the list of confirmed superconductors - because a lab actually made them.

stories.headline: Generated Video Falls Apart After a Few Seconds. A Training-Free Method Stretches It to Two Minutes.
stories.key_takeaway: A training-free inference-time trick called Spectral Self-Anchoring extends a model trained on five-second clips to stable two-minute generation for about 16.5 percent extra latency - but reports no FVD or human-preference numbers.

pull_quote.text: The rolling KV cache only retains recent imperfect frames, which deviate significantly from the initially generated high-quality frames, and this mechanism ultimately leads to visual collapse.

stories.article_excerpt: Ask a modern video model for five seconds and you often get something close to photoreal. Ask for a full minute and you can watch it die.

stories.headline: Colorado Wrote America's First AI Law, Then Repealed It Before It Ever Took Effect
stories.key_takeaway: Colorado repealed the core of its first-in-the-nation AI Act via SB 26-189, signed May 14, swapping algorithmic-discrimination duties for a disclosure regime effective January 2027 - after two delays, an xAI lawsuit and DOJ intervention.

pull_quote.text: Everybody lost and everybody won. We still have consumer protections. It's not as much as I would have liked. We're still the only state in the country to pass this legislation.
pull_quote.role: Colorado Senate Majority Leader, sponsor of both bills

data_points.label: Days the original law was in force

stories.article_excerpt: Colorado's landmark AI statute never regulated anyone. Signed in 2024 as the nation's first comprehensive state AI law, it was postponed twice, sued, and finally repealed by the legislature that wrote it.

stories.headline: Germany's Machine Builders Want Europe to Treat Humanoid Robots as Industrial Policy
stories.key_takeaway: VDMA's call to put humanoid robotics at the top of Europe's political agenda is a position statement, not a costed programme - it names no subsidy or local-content rule, and the hardest gap it points at is component dependency on Japanese reducers and Chinese magnets.

pull_quote.text: Germany and Europe must establish a comprehensive value chain featuring domestic production of critical components.

stories.article_excerpt: Read closely, the August 19 statement is a position, not a policy paper. It names no subsidy instrument, no procurement quota, no local-content threshold.

stories.headline: OpenAI Cut Its Cheapest Model by 80 Percent and Reset the Floor Under Inference Pricing
stories.key_takeaway: OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Luna 80 percent to 20 cents per million input tokens on July 30, but disclosed only a 20 percent serving-cost improvement - meaning most of the cut is surrendered margin, not passed-through efficiency.

pull_quote.text: GPT-5.6 Luna is the closest we've come to intelligence too cheap to meter. I've never seen a model this affordable be this powerful.
pull_quote.role: President and Head of AI, Replit

stories.article_excerpt: The cheapest way to run a frontier-lab model through OpenAI's API is now 20 cents per million input tokens. It was one dollar until July 30.

stories.headline: Ornith-1.5 Writes Its Own Homework, and Lands on Claude Opus's Doorstep
stories.key_takeaway: Ornith released three MIT-licensed open-weight models on August 19 whose 397B flagship posts 86.1 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 against Claude Opus 4.8's 85.0 - but every figure is vendor-reported and the models are post-trained on Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4 bases.

pull_quote.text: Rather than relying on a fixed set of human-curated tasks and manually designed harnesses, Ornith-1.5 continuously generates new training tasks, discovers effective strategies for solving them, and improves the policy through reinforcement learning.

stories.article_excerpt: An outfit almost nobody had heard of two months ago published three open-weight models on August 19 and put a number on the board that frontier labs have spent the year defending.

stories.headline: A 65,000-Parameter Model Beats Frontier LLMs at Finding Which Agent Broke
stories.key_takeaway: A University of Illinois team shows agent failure attribution does not need LLM reasoning: a 65,000-parameter graph neural network trained in 1.1 hours tops fine-tuned 14B models and frontier systems, running roughly 300x faster - though absolute accuracy stays under 20 percent.

pull_quote.text: Is heavy LLM reasoning necessary for agent failure attribution?

stories.article_excerpt: When a team of AI agents botches a task, someone has to work out which agent broke it. The field's reflex answer has been to throw another language model at the wreckage.
